name: Vision-Based Mobile App GUI Testing: A Survey
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: Surveys vision-based mobile app GUI testing across test generation, record-and-replay and testing frameworks, drawing on 271 papers including 92 vision-based studies.

name: PC Agent: While You Sleep, AI Works -- A Cognitive Journey into Digital World

summary: Combines PC Tracker interaction capture, completion of action and reasoning annotations, and planning and grounding agents for desktop workflows.

name: Explorer: Robust Collection of Interactable GUI Elements
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Explorer collects interactable GUI elements from a live target application and records user sessions for application-specific model training. It links repeated interface states into a navigation map that supports path planning and voice-directed interaction.

name: GUIrilla: A Scalable Framework for Automated Desktop UI Exploration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUIrilla systematically explores macOS interfaces to collect interaction traces and accessibility metadata for downstream GUI research. It organizes these observations into hierarchical MacApp Trees and describes an accessibility-driven collection library.

name: ShowUI-Aloha: Human-Taught GUI Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Transforms human screen recordings and input events into annotated demonstrations used by planning and execution components for GUI tasks.

name: cotomi Act: Learning to Automate Work by Watching You
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its reported task score uses the 179-task WebArena human-evaluation subset.
summary: cotomi Act is a browser agent that executes multi-step tasks and turns observed user browsing into persistent knowledge shared with users.

name: Known By Their Actions: Fingerprinting LLM Browser Agents via UI Traces
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported identification results come from four web environments.
summary: A study shows that websites can infer the model behind a browser agent from passively recorded UI actions and timing traces across web tasks.

name: CutVerse: A Compositional GUI Agents Benchmark for Media Post-Production Editing
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Cutverse benchmarks GUI agents on long editing workflows across professional media applications and parses recordings and input logs into grounded action trajectories.

name: Demo2Tutorial: From Human Experience to Multimodal Software Tutorials
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces Demo2Tutorial, which turns recorded software interactions into multimodal tutorials with task graphs and reports benefits for GUI-agent planning.

name: AppAgent-Claw: CLI Is All You Need for GUI Automation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces AppAgent-Claw, which records demonstrated GUI workflows as reusable OpenClaw skills, locates visual targets during replay and checks intended on-screen effects.

name: Syll: Open-Source Personal Automation with Cross-Surface Execution
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Syll combines tool calls, shell execution and visual GUI control in a personal-automation runtime. It turns user demonstrations into reusable skills and exposes execution logs, keyframes and approval checkpoints for inspection.

name: PreAct: Computer-Using Agents that Get Faster on Repeated Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: PreAct compiles successful screen-interaction runs into guarded state-machine programs for repeated tasks. It validates programs from clean states before storage and returns control to the agent when replayed screen expectations fail, with tests across mobile, desktop and web.

name: HANSEL: Extracting Breadcrumbs from Web Agent Trajectories for Interactive Verification
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: HANSEL extracts evidence pages and snippets from browser-agent traces and preserves relevant page state in interactive verification views. It flags untraceable answers and evaluates evidence selection and human verification effort separately.

name: Activity Frames: Deterministic Screen-Activity Compilation for Agent Memory and Replay
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported capture analysis uses one professional's single-user corpus.
summary: Introduces Activity Frames, a deterministic pipeline that turns captured screen activity into typed episodes for computer-use agent memory and routine replay.

name: LegacyWorld: Atomicity-Aware Evaluation of GUI Agents for Legacy Workflows
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: LegacyWorld evaluates Windows GUI workflows under an atomicity criterion: finish correctly or fail without persistent unintended changes. It compares expert prompts with prompts derived from recorded golden paths and separates useful completion, safe failure and non-atomic side effects.

name: Inducing Task Models from Computer-Use Traces
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Task Model Induction disentangles concurrent activities in screenshot and mouse/keyboard traces, then constructs hierarchical goals and procedural control flow for each task. Evaluation tests reconstruction of observed execution and reuse of derived skills on held-out tasks.

name: OmegaUse-SOP: SOP Engineering for Professional Computer Use from Human Demonstrations
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: OmegaUse-SOP converts expert GUI demonstrations into configurable procedures and refines them with domain rules and human input. It records, abstracts, grounds and verifies live execution, with a case study of photovoltaic simulation workflows in PVsyst 7.2.

name: Work2Skill: Capturing Human GUI Experience for Reusable Agent Skill Induction

summary: Aligns human screen recordings, input events, and accessibility information to derive reusable workflow skills from desktop demonstrations.

name: Shadow
notes: Requires Apple Silicon, macOS 14 or later and a source build (Swift 6, Rust, XcodeGen). GroundingOracle.swift resolves targets for the Mimicry replay system in four steps: exact accessibility-tree match, fuzzy accessibility match, a local ShowUI-2B model on MLX over a live screenshot, then a vision-model escalation. TrainingDataGenerator.swift turns recorded (screenshot, accessibility state, click) tuples into JSONL grounding examples, and LoRATrainer.swift fine-tunes ShowUI-2B on them through the mlx-vlm Python package once enough new tuples accumulate. The README describes the capture of fourteen signal types, on-device Qwen and Whisper models, a 26-tool agent runtime, and points to a separate computer-use engine from the same publisher for full computer use. Cloud model features are optional with the user's own API key. Code was read, not run.

name: AI Mime
notes: Requires macOS 13 or newer, Python 3.12 and Accessibility, Screen Recording and Input Monitoring permissions; Windows is not supported yet. The recorder (pynput listeners and mss screenshots) writes a manifest of clicks, typing, hotkeys and scrolls with pre-action screenshots, plus optional extract and detail notes. Reflection turns the trace into a coordinate-free schema.json; an optimizer writes optimized_plan.json, preferring script steps, then browser_harness steps (Chrome CDP through a browser-harness git submodule), then ui_agent steps; a build agent packages a Claude Skill-compatible folder with run.sh, inputs and a fallback plan. The ui_agent drives the Mac in the foreground through cua-computer-server MCP tools, which AI Mime extends with combined screenshot-plus-accessibility-tree reads, and is told to target accessibility elements before screenshot coordinates. Agent runtimes are Anthropic (Claude Code) or OpenAI (Codex), selected during onboarding, with custom providers in user_config.yml. A prebuilt macOS DMG is linked from the README. Code was read, not run.

name: native-devtools-mcp
notes: Distributed through npm (npx native-devtools-mcp; version 0.10.1 in npm/package.json and Cargo.toml at the inspected commit) and as a signed macOS app for Claude Desktop. On macOS it can walk the Accessibility tree and dispatch AXPress, value and selection changes without moving the cursor (src/macos/ax.rs), besides CGEvent input and Vision OCR; Windows uses SendInput, UI Automation and Windows Media OCR. Chrome and Electron pages are driven through the Chrome DevTools Protocol with chromiumoxide (src/cdp/mod.rs), and Android through adb shell input and uiautomator (src/android/input.rs). Optional start_recording captures window frames and hover tracking reports dwell-filtered pointer positions with the element under them (src/tools/hover_tracker.rs). The README states that Linux and iOS are not supported. The server contains no model or agent loop; an MCP client supplies the agent. Code was read, not run.
summary: Local Rust MCP server for operating macOS and Windows apps, Chrome or Electron pages over CDP, and Android devices over ADB, with screenshots, OCR, accessibility lookup, input and template matching.

name: Browse AI
notes: The help center describes two ways to train a robot: Table Studio, where AI builds the data table from a URL, and Robot Studio, where the user shows the robot what to capture through visual point-and-click training; the llms.txt file also lists a Chrome extension for robot training. Trained robots mimic a user to sign in with stored credentials, fill forms and searches, click buttons, toggles and dropdowns, paginate and scroll, capture screenshots and run on schedules or in bulk, and the llms.txt file states cloud-based execution. The interactions serve data extraction and change monitoring. Prices, usage figures and reliability are publisher statements and were not independently tested.
summary: No-code web scraping and monitoring platform whose robots replay recorded clicks, typed inputs, dropdown choices, logins and pagination on target sites, or let AI build the table, then extract data on a schedule.

name: Retriever AI (rtrvr.ai)
notes: Retriever AI describes its engine as DOM-native: a planner directs sub-agents for clicks, typing and navigation, DOM extraction, pagination and files, and the same agent runs in the Chrome extension, in Cloud headless browsers (logins carried over by Cookie Sync) and through the API. Free Mode includes supported models and cloud browser time with sponsored cards and a daily allowance; users can bring their own model keys, and schedules, triggers, Cookie Sync and API or MCP control of the user's own Chrome require a paid plan. Recordings capture DOM interactions and the page's own network calls rather than the screen, and can be turned into replays or into subroutines that call a site's endpoints directly. An experimental Jev option lets a separate model choose browser actions while the selected model plans. The company also offers Rover, an agent that site owners embed for their visitors, and sells browser-agent trajectories and replica business apps for evaluation. The homepage's Web Bench ranking claim and reliability were not independently tested.
summary: Browser agent from Retriever AI that runs in a Chrome extension on the user's signed-in sessions or in cloud browsers, reading page structure to click, type and fill forms; also callable through an API and MCP.

name: Komos
notes: The documentation describes a task as a reusable automation graph. Its Agent Action node handles browser steps (navigating, clicking, filling forms, scrolling, extracting) from a natural-language prompt, can also call integrations and inspect captured network requests, and accepts screenshots as visual references. A task can be trained from a narrated screen or tab recording of up to five minutes, which Komos turns into a plan, or built step by step in a visual builder. Runs use a fresh or persistent cloud Chromium sandbox on Daytona compute, or a self-hosted runner on a Windows or macOS host that can reuse SSO sessions; the Chrome extension path is retired. The built-in assistant Moss creates, schedules and debugs tasks from chat and is also reachable from coding agents through an MCP server. The model behind the agent is not stated. Pricing, availability and reliability were not independently tested.
summary: Hosted automation platform whose task flows use a prompt-driven agent to navigate, click, type and extract on websites in a cloud Chromium sandbox or self-hosted runner, built from narrated screen recordings or chat.

name: VideoCUA
notes: At revision 6ecc530d raw_data/ holds one ZIP archive per application, 87 in total and about 26.1 GB. The card describes each archive as task folders with an action_log.json (instruction, platform and timestamped actions) and a 1920x1080 MP4 recording with its metadata; each action carries a groundcua_id that the card says identifies the matching annotated GroundCUA screenshot. Frame extraction into trajectories and LLM-written chain-of-thought steps come from a pipeline in the GroundCUA GitHub repository, so this release holds raw recordings and logs, not reasoning annotations. The card names no operating system. Its license section links a LICENSE file that the repository does not contain; MIT is the card's metadata declaration and does not establish rights to the recorded applications' content. Task, hour and frame figures are publisher-reported; the archives were not downloaded.
summary: Expert desktop computer-use demonstrations from CUA-Suite: 30 fps screen recordings with millisecond-timestamped mouse and keyboard action logs for about 10K tasks in 87 applications.
